references.text: Same context: The officer himself says that he is not worthy (ἱκανός) for Jesus to come under his roof, which stands in contrast to the Jewish elders who say he is worthy (ἄξιος).
The reason the Jewish elders give for why the officer is worthy: he loves the people and has built the synagogue for them.
The parallel account in Matthew about the Roman officer in Capernaum who asks Jesus to help his servant, where Jesus replies that He will come and heal him.
Cornelius, another God-fearing Roman officer, is also spoken of positively by all the Jewish people, in a similar way to how the officer in Luke 7 was recommended by the Jewish elders.
Paul uses the word ἄξιος when he says that those who reject God's word do not consider themselves worthy (ἀξίους) of eternal life—the same concept of worthiness that the elders use here.
Jesus uses ἄξιος regarding finding anyone who is worthy in a town—the same concept of worthiness that the Jewish elders apply to the officer.
Paul urges believers to walk in a manner worthy (ἀξίως) of God—related to the idea of being counted as worthy, just as the officer was by the Jewish elders.
